new_statements.translation: p.55/63: [in the languages of the centre of the island] the tonic accent is very strongly marked on the penultimate syllable and the final vowel is so devoiced as to be barely distinguishable; p.57/65: [after final-vowel loss] stress falls on the last syllable, which was originally the penultimate (e.g. Port Sandwich); the accent is very weakly marked; these changes are attested in all the coastal languages, where unstressed vowels tend to be centralized and raised.

new_statements.relation_note: Contrary to Lynch & Crowley's remark that the atlas has 'no phonological information', vol. 1 pp. 55-57/63-65 contain phonetic notes with explicit stress remarks and segment inventories by language number (e.g. voiced velar fricative in 17 of 19 languages).
new_statements.rule_in_words: South Malakula generally: tonic accent on the penultimate syllable (strong in the centre-of-island languages, with a devoiced final vowel); in all coastal languages the final vowel is being lost so that stress surfaces on the final syllable, historically the penult, and is weakly marked. Nasvang-specific assignment not visible in the snippets.
new_statements.secondary_stress: not mentioned in the snippets seen
new_statements.exceptions: Port Sandwich: very old speakers retain the older (penultimate, vowel-final) forms (snippet truncated); vowel centralization/raising in unaccented syllables in coastal languages; some segment realizations restricted to stressed syllables in Ninde (6), Nahava (7), Naha'aj (8) (p.64-65).
new_statements.identity_note: The atlas covers 19 South Malakula doculects including no. 11 'nasvaŋ-Farun' = Nasvang (Aznar 2019 fn. 216; Lynch & Crowley 2001:75 'the only source for this language'). The prosodic remarks seen are areal (languages 'of the center of the island' = Lendamboi/Letemboi group per Lynch & Crowley 2001:72 fn; 'all coastal languages', e.g. Port Sandwich); whether Nasvang is named in either group could not be seen.
